title: Staggered usage accumulator with SLA-aware throttling for reserved capacity
creator: Sofia Patel
description:
Problem: Reserved customers occasionally observe abrupt token-level throttles at monthly boundaries or when cross-region failovers occur. The current hard reset behavior creates user-visible spikes (both over-throttling and transient overage) and complicates billing reconciliation for reserved pools.

Goal: Implement a 'staggered usage accumulator' that smooths per-tenant resets across a configurable window while preserving strict per-tenant accounting and SLA headroom guarantees. Key behaviors: (1) allocate monthly commitment to an internal accumulator rather than a sharp epoch reset; (2) apply a staggered decay/crediting schedule per-tenant to avoid synchronized spikes; (3) provide an SLA-aware throttle floor so critical customers never hit sudden denial during short bursts; (4) produce idempotent, auditable journal entries for billing reconciliation and retroactive adjustments.

Why unique: Instead of shifting epoch semantics or inventing ad-hoc holiday rules, the accumulator acts as a lease-backed ledger with deterministic checkpoints. It supports reserved capacity features (burst carveouts, carry-forward, and intra-month transfers) and integrates with existing quota reclaim and preemption flows. The design favors deterministic accounting first, then latency/throughput efficiency via background compaction and low-overhead checkpointing.
acceptance_criteria: No customer sees a >15% spike in throttles at monthly boundary for rolling window customers in internal canaries
Accumulator journals produced for every tenant epoch transition and persisted to the billing store (S3/warehouse) with unique checkpoint IDs
SLA headroom policy enforces guaranteed minimum throughput for P0/P1 reserved tiers during staggered resets
End-to-end reconciliation script matches live usage to billed usage within tolerances for canary tenants (<=0.1% tokens) after two restarts
Feature can be toggled per-tenant and has a safe default off for new tenants
updates: 2025-02-12: Kickoff meeting with billing, infra, and product. Agreed goals and non-goals. Decided to keep ledger append-only for easier audits.
2025-02-18: Prototype accumulator in Go submitted for review. PR: https://github.com/redwood/infra/pull/5198
2025-02-25: Benchmarked accumulator write amplification on dev cluster. Observed 2.3x write rate without compaction; plan to implement background compaction and tombstone sweeps.
2025-03-01: Product reviewed UX gating and rollout strategy. Decided staged rollout by account age and reserved size. Added canary cohort (5 accounts).
2025-03-03: Added journaling schema to map accumulator checkpoints to billing rows; compatibility tests with warehouse ETL completed locally.
review_feedback: From Priya (Billing): Ensure accumulator journals are immutable and include a signature/hash to detect post-facto edits.
From Tomas (Runtime): Prefer lease-backed in-memory checkpoints to reduce coordinator load; Marcus to prototype TTL-based leases.
From Hannah (Legal): Add audit fields for KMS key IDs and data retention policy; follow-up for compliance review requested.
implementation_notes: Core data structure: append-only per-tenant accumulator with (checkpoint_id, epoch_ts, delta_tokens, source) records
Reset semantics: rather than zeroing counters at boundary, credit next epoch according to stagger schedule computed from tenant hash + configurable jitter window
Throttling policy: read-only fast path checks an in-memory SLA floor; if near-floor, route to slow path that consults accumulator journal for precise allowance
Reconciliation: nightly compaction job produces a canonical snapshot for downstream billing; snapshots are idempotent and referenced by checkpoint_id
Rollback plan: feature flag with 'drain' mode to migrate accumulators back to classical epoch counters and emit compensating journal entries
